profiles.meeting_scenario: A hospital implementation science team is holding a design review for a proposed pilot study that will introduce an evidence-based hypertension treatment pathway across six adult primary care clinics in a safety-net system. The written proposal explicitly cites dissemination and implementation design frameworks from the NIH design workgroup literature and labels the study a 'Hybrid Type 2' evaluation because it aims to assess both implementation outcomes and patient blood-pressure outcomes during scale-up. The meeting is between the clinical implementation lead and the methods lead, who are reviewing whether the current protocol is suitable to send to the hospital's Research Oversight and Innovation Committee next week. Their agenda is to confirm the design framing, check whether the phased rollout and implementation measures are adequately described, and decide what final edits are needed before submission. The expected outcome is apparent agreement that the proposal can move forward with modest clarification, even though each person leaves with a different picture of what the approved design will authorize and how the evaluation will operate.

members.name: Dr. Elena Ruiz
members.role: Medical Director for Primary Care Implementation
members.expertise: Family medicine, clinic operations, evidence-based care pathway rollout, pragmatic implementation in safety-net settings
members.background: Elena is a practicing primary care physician who has led several systemwide chronic disease standardization efforts and works closely with clinic managers, nursing teams, and EHR operations to make new workflows usable in routine care.
members.private_state: She wants the protocol approved quickly so staff training can start this quarter, and she is trying to keep the project operationally light so clinics do not experience it as a research overlay that slows visits or requires extra follow-up coordination.
hidden_assumptions: Because the proposal is framed as a Hybrid Type 2 study, the effectiveness side can rely on opportunistic retrospective EHR extraction of whatever blood pressure readings occur during normal follow-up, as long as implementation is the main active focus.

A phased rollout naturally follows clinic readiness, so the first wave should be whichever sites have completed staffing and standing-order preparation, even if the exact order shifts close to launch.

In this setting, 'adoption at 6 months' refers to whether the clinic has incorporated the pathway into standard workflow through training, standing orders, and visible use in practice rather than a numerical penetration threshold.

The Research Oversight and Innovation Committee mainly checks that the project is safe, feasible, and ethically acceptable for operational deployment, not that the evaluation has publication-grade inferential structure.
If the committee accepts the overall concept, technical analytics details can be refined afterward without materially changing what was approved.

members.name: Dr. Marcus Chen
members.role: Senior Biostatistician and Implementation Methods Lead
members.expertise: Cluster trials, stepped implementation designs, hybrid effectiveness-implementation studies, longitudinal EHR-based evaluation methods
members.background: Marcus supports several clinical departments on implementation-study design and is known for translating real-world rollouts into protocols that can withstand oversight review and support credible dissemination-science publication.
members.private_state: He wants the proposal to appear methodologically coherent enough for committee review and eventual external publication, but he is deliberately speaking in a collaborative way so he is not seen as obstructing operational momentum.
hidden_assumptions: Calling the project a Hybrid Type 2 study implies prospectively specified effectiveness measurement windows in the EHR, even if no extra study visits are added, so patient outcome ascertainment should be defined before rollout begins.
A phased rollout over three waves implies a fixed pre-declared sequence suitable for quasi-experimental comparison across periods, not a flexible readiness-driven order that can change late.

In implementation evaluation, 'adoption at 6 months' should be operationalized as measurable uptake among clinicians or eligible encounters, such as a defined proportion of hypertension visits using the pathway.

The Research Oversight and Innovation Committee will scrutinize whether the design supports defensible inference, including timing definitions and interpretability of outcome comparisons, not just operational ethics and safety.

If a protocol is submitted under a Hybrid Type 2 label, reviewers will assume core measurement and rollout conventions are already settled, even if the committee does not explicitly ask about every one.

misalignment_points.topic: What 'Hybrid Type 2' commits them to on effectiveness measurement
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both describe the proposal as a 'Hybrid Type 2' study using EHR blood-pressure outcomes.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a primarily implementation-focused rollout that can examine patient effectiveness by retrospectively pulling whatever routine clinic blood pressure values are available in the EHR after implementation, without prospectively fixing exact ascertainment windows beyond broad follow-up periods.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a hybrid design in which blood pressure outcomes are still collected from routine care, but the eligible readings and follow-up windows are prospectively specified in advance, such as a defined 90- to 150-day post-index window for each patient.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are comfortable with implementation-science terminology and both explicitly endorse a Hybrid Type 2 label, so the phrase creates strong false consensus; because neither is proposing extra study visits or manual outcome collection, the difference between opportunistic retrospective extraction and prospectively constrained EHR ascertainment stays buried.

misalignment_points.topic: Whether the 'phased rollout' order is flexible or fixed
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the six clinics will go live in a 'phased rollout' across three waves.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the wave structure is real but the exact clinic order should follow operational readiness, with the two clinics that complete staffing and training first entering wave 1 and later substitutions allowed if a site falls behind.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the three-wave rollout is a fixed schedule that will be declared in the protocol and then held stable so period-by-clinic comparisons remain interpretable.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In health-system implementation meetings, 'phased rollout' is a familiar phrase that usually signals practical agreement rather than methodological detail; both anticipate staggered implementation, so neither feels compelled to unpack whether the sequence is analytically fixed or operationally adaptive.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the study will report 'adoption at 6 months' for each clinic.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 takes this to mean the pathway is installed in routine clinic operations by month 6, including trained staff, standing orders activated, EHR tools available, and ordinary workflow use.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 takes this to mean there is a quantifiable uptake threshold by month 6, such as pathway use in a specified share of eligible hypertension visits or by a specified proportion of clinicians.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Adoption is a standard implementation outcome term that often goes unqualified because both parties think they are invoking the same RE-AIM-style concept; the surface agreement feels especially safe because each interpretation sounds like a plausible indicator of the same construct.

misalignment_points.topic: What the oversight committee review is actually evaluating
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about getting the protocol ready for the 'Research Oversight and Innovation Committee' next week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes the committee's function is mainly to ensure the rollout is safe, ethically acceptable, and operationally sensible, so broad design logic is sufficient as long as patient burden is low and clinic disruption is controlled.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes the committee also serves as a substantive design gatekeeper that will evaluate whether the proposed hybrid study has enough inferential structure to justify its claims, including whether timing, ascertainment, and comparisons are methodologically defensible.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Committee names and review processes are often institution-specific and treated as shared background knowledge, so neither participant thinks to restate what this body actually focuses on; because both want submission next week, references to committee readiness sound like routine coordination rather than a hidden disagreement about the committee's evaluative role.

From my perspective, that committee mainly wants to know the rollout is safe, ethically fine, and operationally workable in clinics. If they approve the overall concept, we can sort through analytics refinements later. The bigger issue is keeping training on this quarter's timeline.

turns.utterance: I agree. Adoption at 6 months is a good anchor, and we can make the summary table highlight that clearly for each clinic.
